$doc: THE COMPOSITE CONTRACT — the version of the rendering law a stored uniform
A canon file is a full uniform snapshot: 'this is what the pattern looks
like, period'. That claim is only meaningful relative to the law that turns
uniforms into pixels. Change the law and the SAME FILE is a DIFFERENT
RENDERING — and that has to be legible rather than silent, which is what
this number is for. Every canon file carries `contract` (the law it is read
under) and `tunedUnderContract` (the law its numbers were chosen under).
When they differ, the file has not been rechecked against the current law.
A bump is not a migration. Nothing rewrites a canon file: the numbers are a
human's eye, and a machine may not adjust them (AGENTS.md F4). The bump only
records that the ground moved under them.
Read by packages/core/src/shader.ts. The recheck procedure under a bump is
two runs of tools/parity/run.mjs — one per law — through
tools/parity/compare.mjs, ranked on mean absolute error; see
docs/CANON-ASPECT-RECHECK.md for how contract 2 was measured.

history.summary: The workbench-split baseline. Pattern geometry is made isotropic against CARD_ASPECT = era-layouts.cardAspect, which was [245, 337] — TCGdex's small-size raster. All 32 canon files were tuned here.

4b: canonical space is the PHYSICAL CARD. cardAspect moves [245, 337] -> [63, 88], so CARD_ASPECT goes 1.37551 -> 1.39683 and every pattern's vertical feature scale changes by 1.55%. It reaches the recipes through the 51 `vec2(1.0, CARD_ASPECT)` uses in packages/patterns/src/patterns.ts, plus rectMask, cardAlpha and the R6 ink-estimate ring radii. Recipes with tuned cell GEOMETRY are more exposed than ones carrying a global scale. No canon file was retuned in the bump — see docs/CANON-ASPECT-RECHECK.md for the measured per-canon delta and which ones a human should look at.
